paragraphs.source_en: He nevertheless acknowledged that the reading of superimpositions is difficult because of the different states of erosion in various sites. The most resistant colours, white and red, appear to be fresher than other colours such as yellow or green. The different preservation is also caused by dissimilar binding material with variable resistance. If recent images made with poor quality colours and bindings were painted over older images made of colour with a very strong binding material, the poor colour would not adhere on the earlier paintings and the superimpositions would appear chronologically inverted (Sansoni 1994).

units.source_en: He nevertheless acknowledged that the reading of superimpositions is difficult because of the different states of erosion in various sites.
The most resistant colours, white and red, appear to be fresher than other colours such as yellow or green.
The different preservation is also caused by dissimilar binding material with variable resistance.

If recent images made with poor quality colours and bindings were painted over older images made of colour with a very strong binding material, the poor colour would not adhere on the earlier paintings and the superimpositions would appear chronologically inverted (Sansoni 1994).

paragraphs.source_en: The other problem in assessing the relative chronology within the Round Head complex is the repainting of the oldest figures or parts of figures with new colours, so that older images seem to be more recent. Moreover, some styles have been used throughout the whole period and some, on the contrary, are represented only by a few figures in a single shelter. In the chronological-stylistic assessment Sansoni (1994) also uses the position of the figures on the wall. He claims that the most ancient figures occupy the central part of the wall and the successive images were located in the free spaces next, above or below the previous paintings. This method presumes that painters always started to paint in the centre of the wall, which is perhaps questionable.

paragraphs.source_en: Sansoni thus proposes that the art be divided into the archaic, medium, evolved, declining and very evolved periods, each represented by different styles. It is also controversial in that the respective styles are very similar and any distinction is therefore highly subjective. Indeed, what one author places into the archaic phase another author may place into the medium or evolved one. The main reason for this disagreement seems to be the fact that various authors have concentrated on a limited number of painted sites with different orders of superimpositions of respective styles. Sansoni's division seems plausible only in terms of an archaic, a medium and an evolved phase.
